title: Ibovespa Jumps Ahead of Election
body: The Ibovespa surged 2.6% to close at 192,114 in a highly volatile session ahead of Sunday's first-round elections. The index opened with strong gains, supported by a favorable external backdrop, then gave back those advances on renewed political risk before recovering into the close. With the vote approaching, demand for hedging remains elevated. When markets reopen on Monday, the election outcome, the new composition of Congress, and early signals on fiscal policy are expected to play a larger role in the pricing of Brazilian assets. Externally, oil prices declined after the G7 agreed to release strategic reserves to ease mounting fuel costs, tempering concerns about energy-driven inflation. In addition, softer-than-expected US payrolls data supported credit-sensitive stocks as the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month diminished. Financials advanced, with Bradesco gaining 3.2%. Utilities were also higher, led by a 2.8% rise in Axia. Among blue chips, Petrobras climbed 2.8%, WEG added 3.8%, and Rede D'Or rose 3.6%. For the week, the Ibovespa was up 4.7%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: TSX Advances as Oil Rally Stalls
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index climbed 1% to close at 35,503 as the recent oil rally lost momentum, easing worries about energy-driven inflation and driving Canadian bond yields lower. Softer-than-expected US payroll data further supported rate-sensitive sectors, with markets dialing back expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike this month. Financials advanced, led by a 1.1% gain in CIBC and a 2% rise in Great-West Lifeco. Technology shares also moved higher, mirroring strength in the Wall Street AI trade: Shopify added 1.7%, while Celestica jumped 3.9%. Mining stocks rose despite a pullback in gold prices, as the weaker US jobs report tempered Fed tightening expectations and improved the outlook for the metal. Agnico Eagle gained 2.1%, and WPM rose 2.6%. On the policy front, Prime Minister Carney announced that Canada will fast-track approval for a proposed crude oil export pipeline to the West Coast, a project seen as central to efforts to diversify the country's economy away from its heavy reliance on the United States. title: Wall Street Gains on Soft Jobs Report
body: US stock indices finished higher on Friday after a weaker-than-expected jobs report led investors to scale back expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening. The S&P 500 advanced 0.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose by 250 points, and the Nasdaq gained 1% to close at a record high of 30,808. Nonfarm payrolls increased by just 29,000 in the latest month, far below the consensus forecast of a 90,000 gain. Payroll figures for the prior two months were also revised lower. Following the data, market-based expectations for additional Fed rate hikes eased. Oil prices declined, lending support to the bond market and providing an additional tailwind for equities. Credit-sensitive stocks moved higher, and AI-related companies—despite facing record levels of debt issuance—also finished mostly in positive territory. Nvidia climbed 1.3%, Broadcom rose 3.3%, and AMD gained 2.9%. Among the major cloud providers, Alphabet added 1.6%, Amazon advanced 1.3%, and Oracle increased 3.1%. Tesla jumped 4.6% after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter sales. For the week, the S&P 500 edged up 0.2% and the Nasdaq rose 1.3%, while the Dow shed 319 points. Because the profile is calculated over a completed historical range, I would describe this as the prior quarter's value-area-high zone, rather than a "developing" value area high. That distinction matters because INTC's latest rebound has so far failed before reaching that zone. The stock closed at $119.33 on October 2, leaving it roughly 8% below the lower edge of the $128.75-$130.75 area. In other words, buyers have not yet tested what appears to have been the upper boundary of the market's previous high-volume acceptance area. This strengthens the caution already visible in the recent price action.

title: Vietnam Q3 GDP Growth Strongest Since 2022
body: Vietnam's economy expanded by 9.95% year-on-year in Q3 2026, accelerating from a revised 8.81% in Q2 and marking the fastest pace since Q3 2022. All major sectors recorded robust growth. Industry and construction jumped 12.50%, contributing 51.57% of total value added. Services increased 9.54%, accounting for 43.29%, while agriculture grew 4.21%, representing 5.14%. On the expenditure side, final consumption rose 8.96%, and fixed investment surged 21.39%. In external trade, exports of goods and services increased 23.27%, while imports advanced 28.75%. Over the first three quarters of 2026, GDP expanded by 9.01%. Vietnam is aiming for full-year economic growth of more than 10%, underpinned by higher infrastructure spending. In comparison, the economy grew 8.02% in 2025. On September 23, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast for Vietnam to 7.8% from 7.2%, while cautioning that heightened global uncertainty could weigh on exports, investment, and the exchange rate. title: S&P 500 technical analysis as week ended less than 1% lower than ATH just shy of 7850
body: S&P 500 futures test whether the channel breakout can hold S&P 500 E-mini futures have improved after breaking out of the broader descending channel that contained much of the August-to-September pullback. But the four-hour chart is now at the more interesting stage: not whether price can briefly rise above resistance, but whether buyers can keep it there. After reaching 7,848.50 on September 22, ES pulled back through a sequence of lower highs and eventually fell to apx 7,672 on October 1. The rebound from that low has been sharp. Price reached 7,810.25 on October 2 before finishing the latest four-hour bar at 7,776.50. That puts ES around the shorter descending trendline drawn from the September high. The move above it is encouraging, but still looks more like an early breakout attempt than a completed breakout. The rejection from 7,810 is important because it shows that sellers are still responding above the trendline. Momentum has improved alongside the recovery. MACD has crossed back above its signal line and moved above zero, while the additional trend evidence in the supplied data has also shifted upward. Volume during the earlier part of the October 2 advance was relatively strong compared with similar time periods, although follow-through later in the session was less impressive. Volatility has also expanded, with the four-hour average trading range rising from the high-20s toward roughly 35 points.
